title: The Jack Benny Program
paragraphs: Mixed historical subset showing Jack Benny’s evolution from sponsor-led musical/variety programs in 1932-34 to the ensemble situation-comedy/variety format of the 1941-42 Jell-O season. The frozen 51-object GRH container is not a continuous run.

GRH documents the program through Canada Dry Program (May 2, 1932 to January 26, 1933) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chevrolet Program season one (March 3, 1933 to June 23, 1933) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chevrolet Program season two (October 1, 1933 to April 1, 1934) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Jell-O Program 1941-42 (October 5, 1941 to May 31, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Jack Benny (performer on 50 recordings), Alois Havrilla (performer on 1 recording), Dennis Day (performer on 1 recording), Don Wilson (announcer on 1 recording), Edward G. Robinson (performer on 1 recording), Humphrey Bogart (performer on 1 recording), and Mahlon Merrick (music on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include sponsor-integrated radio comedy, comic self-caricature and show-business persona, wartime military-service and home-front broadcasting, music and variety performance, Hollywood, movies and show business, and murder-mystery parody.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Pearl Harbor interruption, Carole Lombard memorial replacement, Evolution from musical variety to character-based situation comedy, and Military-base wartime broadcasts.

Mixed historical subset showing Jack Benny’s evolution from sponsor-led musical/variety programs in 1932-34 to the ensemble situation-comedy/variety format of the 1941-42 Jell-O season. The frozen 51-object GRH container is not a continuous run.

GRH documents the program through Canada Dry Program (May 2, 1932 to January 26, 1933) on NBC Radio Network, Chevrolet Program season one (March 3, 1933 to June 23, 1933) on NBC Radio Network, Chevrolet Program season two (October 1, 1933 to April 1, 1934) on NBC Radio Network, and Jell-O Program 1941-42 (October 5, 1941 to May 31, 1942) on NBC Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Jack Benny (performer on 50 recordings), Alois Havrilla (performer on 1 recording), Dennis Day (performer on 1 recording), Don Wilson (announcer on 1 recording), Edward G. Robinson (performer on 1 recording), Humphrey Bogart (performer on 1 recording), and Mahlon Merrick (music on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include sponsor-integrated radio comedy, comic self-caricature and show-business persona, wartime military-service and home-front broadcasting, music and variety performance, Hollywood, movies and show business, and murder-mystery parody.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Pearl Harbor interruption, Carole Lombard memorial replacement, Evolution from musical variety to character-based situation comedy, and Military-base wartime broadcasts.
